rationale_bullets: Becht (80.0/409; 3rd all-time in Cyclone passing) followed Campbell to PSU with his backup - but the replacement is the best-credentialed piece of the rebuild: Raynor (74.5/615; 3,361 @ 66.5%, 19-11; two-time All-SBC; 9,877/67 career), who won the job in spring and imported his own TE.
Flores (58.6/312; 7 INT/3 TD at OkSt) is a real second option with P4 snaps.
PS's attributed read: 'last year's Cyclone pass numbers are attainable for Raynor.'
48 = fringe-average: proven G5 volume + decent tape into a brand-new power-run scheme.
The dynamic duo left (Hansen 950 -> PSU; Sama 732 -> Wisconsin) and the marquee depth add (Allah) tore his Achilles in spring.
What's left: Pettaway (72.8/85; MAC FrOY largely on returns - 365 rush), Flora (return ace, 58 rush yds), Barnes (65.1/90).
A power-rushing OC (Roehl, ex-NDSU) with no returning 400-yard rusher behind a 15-start OL. 42 = below average.
The top EIGHT receivers depart (both 500-yd WRs + both TEs to PSU); Overby is the lone returning rotation piece.
The verified adds are one high-grade small sample (Hayes 83.6/162 from Tulane) + the QB's own TE (Fortenberry 57.0/361) + FCS production with no rows (Jackson-Tarleton).
PS's 'production won't drop much' rests on 2025 already being depressed (top-4 = 1,774). 40, L: eleven transfers, one verified above-average tape.

All five starters gone; the rebuilt line has 15 CAREER FBS STARTS and zero FBS full-time starters (PS) - four of five projected starters have no PFF rows at all (Tarleton FCS-AA Smith, D2 Maas, Montana Amick, injured-2025 Taylor).
Rogers' counter is attributed but unverifiable: 'the deepest O-Line that he has been a part of.'
32 = bottom-sixth: the thinnest verified OL of our round; the FCS-AA pedigree is the upside case.
data_gaps: Zero verifiable tape at 4 of 5 spots

rationale_bullets: The 2025 unit was 1st-pctile as-played with 13 sacks, and its anchor (Orange) was drafted - the floor is fully priced in.

The Wazzu import is real: Terrell (86.8/409 - 7 sk/12 TFL, the round's second-best incoming DL grade), Lamb (69.4/433, 'huge spring reviews'), Ta'ase (68.7/283), Janikowski (72.1/168) - and their system allowed 125 (3.8) with 31 sacks last year.
Hawk + Gilbert are the incumbents; the 4-man-front switch fits the personnel.
46 = fringe-below-average: elite top add onto a terrible baseline, FCS depth behind.
The #1, #2, and #3 tacklers all followed Campbell to PSU from what he'd called his best LB corps in a decade.

The replacements' tape runs behind their framing: Schlimgen ('rising star') at 58.8/308, Willich at 55.9/196; the production stars have no rows (D2 Harlon Hill winner Exline's 143 tackles; FCS-AA Smith). Caution rule leans tape.
40, L: high-variance room - the D2/FCS pedigree could hit, but nothing verified clears average.

rationale_bullets: Top six DBs gone (40 starts) AND the marquee add - Awls (74.3/602; 5 INT, 1st-tm MAC) - tore his ACL in spring.

What remains: M.Jones (70.1/651 JaxSt), pedigree-fading Singletary (64.3/251), Washington (55.0/406), no-row FCS pieces (Harper, S.Johnson, Goodman), incumbents Surges/Coffey; the books disagree on the starting config (battles).
PS's comp is direct: the similarly-built Wazzu '25 secondary finished #66 in his PDR. 40 = below average.

The one improved room: Konrardy returns (14-18 with a SCHOOL-RECORD 63-yarder and a second career 54-yd game-winner vs Iowa; 'one of the best in the country' - Athlon) and the nation's #1 kick returner arrives (Pettaway, 33.0).
Flora (26.1 PR, TD) doubles the return threat; the P job is open (Perkins' 40.8 net departs; Aussie Gurney vs Lounsbury).
SPEC 21st pctile rides the departed punt game; the 2026 K/return core is verified elite. 52 = average-plus.
